title: Can Carpet Be Installed in Winter in Edmonds? Humidity and Stretching
meta: Carpet installs fine in an Edmonds winter if the house is heated, rolls acclimate and the crew power-stretches. Wills Flooring explains humidity and ripples.
keywords: carpet installation in winter, can you install carpet in cold weather, carpet acclimation temperature, carpet installation Edmonds WA, carpet stretching humidity, winter flooring installation

blocks.lead: Yes. Carpet can be installed in any Edmonds winter month, as long as the house is heated to at least 65°F, the rolls sit inside for 24 hours first, and the installer power-stretches rather than knee-kicks.
blocks.detail: Carpet is an indoor product installed in an indoor climate. The rain outside matters far less than the temperature inside your walls, and winter is one of the easiest times to get a crew quickly.

blocks.html: The question usually arrives in January from a homeowner in the Edmonds Bowl or up in Seaview: the old carpet has to go before guests arrive, but it has rained for eleven days straight and the house feels damp. Will the new carpet stretch properly? Will it ripple in June when the heat goes off? Fair questions. The answer is that a heated Edmonds house in February is a normal installation environment.

blocks.text: Why winter carpet installation works in Edmonds

items.title: The work happens at room temperature
items.text: Carpet backing, seam tape and pad adhesive are made to be installed between about 65 and 95°F. Your furnace already holds the house in that range from November to March, so the crew works in July conditions.

items.title: Ferry-town humidity is an outdoor problem
items.text: Edmonds sits on the water and winter air outside hovers near 90 percent relative humidity. Inside a heated home it drops to 30 to 50 percent, which is where carpet fiber and latex backing behave most predictably.

items.title: Crews have open days
items.text: Flooring demand peaks from April through September and again before Thanksgiving. A January or February install in Edmonds often books within a week or two.

items.title: Ramblers heat evenly
items.text: The 1950s to 1970s ramblers in Westgate and Perrinville are single-story with a central furnace, so every room reaches temperature quickly. Split-levels need the daylight basement heated a day early.

blocks.text: Stretching in cold weather: the part that matters

blocks.html: Carpet is a textile with a latex or polyurethane backing. Cold backing is stiff and stretches less for the same force. If an installer stretches a cold carpet only as far as it wants to go that afternoon, the carpet relaxes as the house warms in spring, and the slack shows up as ripples by June. The fix is acclimation plus a power stretcher.

items.text: Rolls arrive wrapped from a heated warehouse and go straight into the room being carpeted, not the garage.
items.note: An Edmonds garage in January is 40°F. That is storage, not acclimation.

items.text: Carpet and pad rest at room temperature so the backing softens and factory curl relaxes. The thermostat stays at 65 to 75°F through two days after install.

A power stretcher braces against the far wall and pulls the carpet about 1 to 1.5 percent each way before it hooks the tack strip. A knee kicker alone cannot reach that tension in anything bigger than a closet.
items.note: This is the single step that prevents summer ripples.

items.text: Keep the heat steady and run the bath fan or crack one window a few hours a day so odor clears and the backing settles.

blocks.text: When you should wait for spring

a.title: Go ahead in winter when
items: The house is occupied and heated every day
Subfloor meters dry and the crawlspace vapor barrier is intact
You want a crew within a couple of weeks
Rooms are upstairs or on a main floor over a crawlspace

b.title: Wait or fix first when
items: The home is vacant and you cannot run the heat for three days
A basement slab shows active moisture or smells musty after rain
A leak, gutter overflow or roof repair is still in progress
Drywall mud or paint is still drying in the rooms

blocks.title: Vacant house warning:
blocks.text: A common Edmonds mistake is carpeting an empty listing with the thermostat at 50°F to save money. The carpet installs stiff, the buyer turns the heat to 70, and the hallway ripples by summer. Run the heat at 65°F for two days before and after.
Winter mistakes we get called to fix

items.html: Knee-kicker-only installs. Cheap crews skip the power stretcher to save time. Cold weather hides how little tension is actually in the carpet.
Rebond pad on a damp slab. Standard bonded urethane soaks up moisture. Daylight basements in Seaview need a moisture-barrier pad if the slab reads high.
Opening every window to air out the smell. Flooding the house with 40°F air drops the rooms below what fresh seams want. Crack one window and use fans.
Ignoring the old pad's story. Water stains on the pad or rusty tack strip mean something is getting wet. Our post on why carpet buckles and ripples shows what a bad stretch looks like a year later.
Set the thermostat to 65 to 70°F two days before delivery and hold it through two days after, including any daylight basement.
Ask for the subfloor moisture reading. Any installer working in Edmonds in winter should carry a meter and tell you the number.
Confirm power stretching in writing. If you are unsure which method you are being sold, read stretch-in vs glue-down carpet.
Plan the path from the driveway. Move cars so the van backs up close and the rolls spend seconds in the rain.
Get the warranty in writing. Wills Flooring covers workmanship for one year, including restretching if an edge loosens. A winter install carries the same warranty as a summer one.

faq.q: What temperature does a house need to be for carpet installation?
faq.a: Aim for 65 to 75°F in every room being carpeted, starting a day or two before the crew arrives and holding for two days after. Below about 60°F the backing stiffens, seam tape bonds poorly and the carpet stretches less than it should.

faq.q: Does Edmonds winter humidity cause carpet to ripple?
faq.a: Outdoor humidity does not. Indoor humidity in a heated Edmonds home is moderate all winter. Ripples come from carpet stretched cold, or with a knee kicker only, that relaxed when the house warmed. Acclimation and a power stretcher prevent it in any month.

faq.q: How long does carpet need to acclimate in winter?
faq.a: Twenty-four hours inside the heated house is the standard. If the rolls came off a cold truck, give them a full day and night. Pad acclimates faster, but let both sit together in the room being carpeted, not in the garage, and keep the thermostat at 65 to 75°F.

faq.q: Can carpet be installed in a cold basement in winter?
faq.a: Yes, if you heat the basement to room temperature for two days first and the slab tests dry. A cool daylight basement is the one place in an Edmonds home where a winter install needs extra care, usually a moisture-barrier pad and longer acclimation.

faq.q: Will new carpet smell worse in winter with the windows closed?
faq.a: The odor is the same, but it clears more slowly without air exchange. Run bath and kitchen fans, crack one window a few hours a day, and pick a low-VOC carpet if anyone is sensitive. Most odor is gone within three to five days.

faq.q: Is winter cheaper for carpet installation in Edmonds?
faq.a: Not on the labor line. Stretch-in is $0.99 per sq ft, glue-down $1.29 and stairs $30 a step in January just as in July. What winter saves is time: scheduling is easier and material lead times are shorter, so a January job usually starts sooner than a June one.
